chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub Al Khazzaz, from Usman Al Nawa’a who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I tend to wash the dead bodies'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'And you are good (at it)?' I said, 'I wash'. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'When you wash, so be gentle with it and neither press it nor touch its ears with camphor; and when you turban him, so do not turban him the turbanning of the Bedouins'. I said, 'How should I do (it)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Take the turban from its middle and display is upon his head, then turn it to its behind, and drop its two ends upon his chest'.
ai.seo_question: What is the proper method for washing and shrouding the deceased according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the ritual etiquette (adab) for washing the deceased, emphasizing physical gentleness and the preservation of dignity through specific shrouding techniques. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) instructs against rough handling, such as pressing the ears with camphor, and prescribes a dignified method of wrapping the headcloth that contrasts with the less refined customs of the Bedouins, reflecting the Shia emphasis on honoring the body as a vessel of the soul.
